title: Ireland Extends Short-Stay Visa Waiver for Indian Travellers to December 31, 2026
excerpt: Eligible Indian passport holders with a qualifying UK short-stay visa can keep visiting Ireland without a separate Irish visa for two more months — but UK residents on long-term permission are not covered.
body:
• Ireland has extended its Short-Stay Visa Waiver Programme from October 31, 2026 to December 31, 2026, under Statutory Instrument No. 541 of 2026.
  • Indian passport holders are among the 21 covered nationalities: with a qualifying UK short-stay visa, you can visit Ireland without applying for a separate Irish visa.
  • You must enter the UK first on that visa. Your stay in Ireland can last up to 90 days, or until your UK immigration permission expires, whichever comes first.
  • The waiver does not cover Indians living in the UK on work, student or other long-term permission over 180 days — they still need an Irish visa.

Ireland will let eligible Indian travellers keep visiting on a UK visa for two more months. The Short-Stay Visa Waiver Programme, which was due to expire on October 31, 2026, now continues until December 31, 2026, according to Ireland's official programme guidance from Immigration Service Delivery.

Who is affected — exactly

The programme covers nationals of 21 countries, including India, China, Indonesia, Kazakhstan, the Philippines, Thailand, Uzbekistan and Vietnam, alongside countries in Eastern Europe, South America and the Middle East, Travel Trade Journal reported. It applies only to short stays: tourism and short business visits on a qualifying UK visa.

Two groups are not covered. First, anyone living in the UK on long-term permission — a work visa, a student visa or leave of more than 180 days — cannot use the waiver and must apply for an Irish visa instead, although the programme guidance provides an exemption from the visa application fee for covered nationals in that position. Second, UK visas issued for transit or for marriage or civil partnership are excluded.

How the waiver works

The mechanism matters, because the order of travel decides whether the waiver applies. You must first travel to the United Kingdom and be admitted on your qualifying UK short-stay visa, with permission of up to 180 days. Only after that UK entry can you travel on to Ireland without a separate Irish visa. Your Irish stay can run for up to 90 days, but it must end before your UK permission expires, whichever date comes first.

If you hold a valid UK visa but have not yet used it to enter the UK, you generally still need an Irish visa to visit Ireland first. The waiver is a UK-first arrangement, not a two-country visa.

Not the same as the British-Irish Visa Scheme

The waiver is frequently confused with the British-Irish Visa Scheme (BIVS), and they are different arrangements. Under BIVS, a single visa endorsed "BIVS" lets an eligible traveller visit both countries, in either order. BIVS is available only to Indian nationals living in India and Chinese nationals living in China at the time of application. The Short-Stay Visa Waiver, by contrast, works off an ordinary qualifying UK short-stay visa and requires the UK leg to come first.

What to do next

If you are planning a combined UK-Ireland trip in November or December 2026, check three things before booking: that your UK visa is a qualifying short-stay visit or business visa, that your itinerary enters the UK before Ireland, and that your Irish stay ends on or before December 31, 2026 and within your UK permission. Travellers whose trips fall after December 31 should not assume a further extension: the programme guidance states it may be amended at any time, and no extension beyond that date has been announced. Full conditions are on the Immigration Service Delivery programme document.
